newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.04 pct in speculative trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.04 pct in speculative trade.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.04 percent to end at 1.0458 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market with players speculating in the spot and future markets, dealers said.

Earlier, the Central Bank set a new weaker reais-dollar mini-band between 1.0450 and 1.0500. The mini-band was lowered 0.58 during January and the local currency fell 0.64 percent during the month in the commercial foreign exchange market.
The speculation today was fueled by a fight between players holding short and long positions in the forex future market, dealers said.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0504, off 0.01 percent on the day and 0.52 percent in the month.
In the illegal parallel market, the real ended at 1.085, down 0.28 percent for the day but up 3.13 percent for the month.
Traders said the currency's rise in the parallel market during January was due to a normal increase in the supply of dollars in that market in the begining of the year.
